predecessors.name: Italian Republic (Kingdom of Italy from 1805)
predecessors.text: Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy (Milan), whose Lombard and Venetian lands Austria occupied in April 1814 and received in 1815; the page's infobox names the Kingdom of Italy (Napoleonic) and the Republic…

successors.name: Kingdom of Sardinia
successors.text: Lombardy up to the Mincio, ceded 1859 (via France) at the Treaty of Zurich; the fortresses of Mantua and Peschiera stayed Austrian

successors.name: Kingdom of Italy
successors.text: Venetia and Mantua, ceded 1866 (to France, then to Italy), annexed by plebiscite 21-22 October 1866

ledger.x: 1815: the Congress of Vienna creates the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia for the Austrian crown.
22 March 1848: Milan rises and Radetzky retreats to the Quadrilateral.
March 1848: Venice proclaims the Republic of San Marco and the Veneto towns follow.
23-26 March 1848: Sardinia invades Lombardy.
22-23 April 1848: Nugent's corps takes Udine.
5 May 1848: Nugent's corps enters Belluno.
11-24 June 1848: Austria retakes the Veneto towns.
By 9 August 1848 only Venice remained in insurgent hands.
9 August 1848: the Salasco armistice returns Lombardy.
9 August 1848: the Salasco armistice ends the first campaign (Custoza 25 July).
13 October 1848: Osoppo, the last mainland stronghold, falls.
22-27 August 1849: Venice surrenders.
26 April 1859: the Second Italian War begins.
11-12 July 1859: the Armistice of Villafranca.
Nov 1859: Austria cedes Lombardy.
1859: the capital moves from Milan to Venice.

20-23 June 1866: Italy opens the Third War of Independence; Custoza on 24 June is an Austrian victory, Garibaldi's volunteers reach Bezzecca (Trentino) on 21 July and Italian forces Romans d'Isonzo on 26 July, 'the maximum Italian advance into Friuli'.
12 August 1866: the Armistice of Cormons ends the fighting in Italy ('the Armistice of Cormons signed on 12 August').
October 1866: Venetia passes to Italy.
1866: the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia ends.

wars.name: First Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Austria crushed the Lombard and Venetian risings and Sardinia's two campaigns (Custoza 25 July 1848, armistice 9 August; Novara 23 March 1849); Venice surrendered in August 1849.

wars.name: Second Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Franco-Sardinian victory at Magenta (4 June) and Solferino (24 June); armistice of Villafranca 11-12 July; Treaty of Zurich: Lombardy to Sardinia via France, Mantua and Legnago (Peschiera) kept by Austria.

wars.name: Third Italian War of Independence
wars.outcome: Italy lost Custoza (24 June) and Lissa (20 July) but obtained Venetia and Mantua through Prussia's victory: Armistice of Cormons 12 August, Peace of Prague, Treaty of Vienna 3 October, cession through France 19 October, plebiscite 21-22 October 1866.

certainty.note: The kingdom's frontiers follow the Congress of Vienna settlement and the provincial boundaries; the page gives no frontier text, so the sharp level rests on the treaty origin.
The insurgents' holdings changed week by week (Milan, Venice, the Veneto towns, Osoppo); the Quadrilateral stayed Austrian throughout.
The 1859 Treaty of Zurich line (the Mincio) and the 1866 Treaty of Vienna cession are treaty lines.
